title: Caring for orphans
hook: two fingers held up, a little apart: that's how close the orphan's carer stands
tomorrow: can a weekly phone call count as a struggle?

segments.voice: Yesterday: a word of truth, said kindly, in the right room. Today the Prophet says something without many words at all. He uses his hand.

Peace sign. Victory sign. Bunny ears behind a friend's head. Two fingers up can mean a lot of things in a photo, and most of them are playful. In one hadith, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ holds up two fingers, his pointing finger and his middle finger, with a little space between them, and the two fingers stand for two people. One of them is him. Who is the other, standing that close?
screen: `TWO FINGERS UP.` → `A LITTLE SPACE BETWEEN.` → `ONE IS HIM. WHO'S THE OTHER?`

segments.voice: The answer is in Sahih al-Bukhari: I and the one who looks after an orphan will be in Paradise like this. And he held up those two fingers, apart a little. That's the distance. Not a row behind. Side by side. Here's why it lands: the Prophet grew up an orphan himself. The Qur'an says it to him directly, in Pickthall's words: "Did He not find thee an orphan and protect (thee)?" A few verses on comes what follows from it: "Therefore the orphan oppress not." The one who was once the child without a father is told: now don't let that child be pushed around. The hadith's word for the carer is kafil: the one who takes responsibility, who has a child's back over time. So caring for an orphan isn't only one grand gesture. Some Muslims sponsor a child far away, and that counts. So does the uncle who takes his brother's kids in, the neighbor who keeps showing up to the school play, the grandmother raising her grandson. One thing worth telling a friend tonight: the man who promised that closeness had been that child first. Two fingers, a small gap. Close enough to touch, and still two.
screen: `THE ORPHAN'S CARER, SIDE BY SIDE.` · `DID HE NOT FIND THEE AN ORPHAN?` · `KAFIL: THE ONE WHO HAS THEIR BACK.` · `STEADY, OVER TIME.` · then, large: `TWO FINGERS TOGETHER.`

segments.voice: Hold up your pointing finger and middle finger, a small space between them, and look at how close they are. Breathing slowly, bring to mind one child you know who is carrying more than a child should. Keep your fingers up as long as it's comfortable, then rest your hand.
screen: `TWO FINGERS, A SMALL GAP.` · `ONE CHILD CARRYING TOO MUCH.` · `REST THE HAND.`

segments.voice: Caring for orphans: taking responsibility for a child who has lost a parent. In the hadith, it puts the carer right beside the Prophet.
Keep this one: two fingers together, close enough to touch, and still two. Goodnight for now.

howItsDone: Muslims care for orphans by taking in relatives' children, sponsoring children through charities, and giving zakat and sadaqah toward their needs; many point to this hadith and the Prophet's own childhood when they do.

options: It matters. The hadith's carer is the one who keeps showing up. Steady counts.
Not much. Real orphan care means paying a child's costs every single month.
Only if you take him in yourself; anything less isn't what the hadith means.
chat.meaning: The hadith's word is kafil, the one who takes responsibility over time. Steady care is the point, and it puts the carer beside the Prophet.
